title: Governance maturity assessment
seo: Power BI and Fabric governance maturity self-assessment: ownership, endorsement, security, lifecycle, monitoring and data quality, with next steps per dimension.
summary: Assess Northwind's BI governance (or your own organisation's) on six dimensions and get the next step for each.
impact: A maturity assessment turns "we should govern better" into a short list of next steps the organisation can actually take this quarter.

body: Before the offsite, score where we are on each governance dimension. Be honest: the point is the next step, not the score. Use your own company instead if you prefer.

evidence.title: From the architecture review (Sprint 10)
body:
- {{s10_no_owner_models|int}} of {{s10_models|int}} models without owner; {{s10_zero_view_reports|int}} of {{s10_reports|int}} reports unused for 90 days.
- {{s10_certified|int}} certified models; {{s10_pipelines|int}} workspaces with deployment pipelines.
- Incident process and on-call alerts exist for certified models only.

interactive.title: Score each dimension from 1 to 5
interactive.intro: Choose the description that is true today, not the one you're planning.

dims.q: Who is responsible for reports and models?
levels: Nobody knows who owns most items.
Owners are known informally for important items.
Every item in production has a named owner in metadata.
Owners review their items periodically; orphaned items are flagged automatically.
Ownership transfers are part of joiner/mover/leaver processes.
next: Run an ownership drive for everything used in the last 90 days.
Record owners in metadata (contact list) and require it to publish.
Add a quarterly owner review using usage and lineage.
Automate orphan detection with the admin APIs.
Keep it: audit ownership changes in HR processes.

dims.q: How are company KPIs defined and served?
levels: Each report defines its own KPIs.
A few shared models exist; KPIs still duplicated.
Certified models serve company KPIs; a KPI dictionary exists.
Certification has criteria and owners; non-certified KPI copies are tracked.
Most consumption runs on certified models; definitions change through a governed process.
next: Pick the top 5 KPIs and write them down with owners.
Certify one shared model for those KPIs.
Publish endorsement criteria and a certification process.
Report certified share of views and chase the copies.
Measure and review definition changes quarterly.

dims.q: How is data access controlled and tested?
levels: Access by sharing links; no RLS testing.
Workspace roles and some RLS.
RLS/OLS in models, groups not individuals, sensitivity labels on sensitive items.
Security test matrices run on every release; access reviewed quarterly.
Least privilege enforced by policy; access anomalies monitored.
next: Move to group-based access and remove broad sharing links.
Add RLS/OLS to sensitive models and label them.
Create a test matrix per sensitive model and run it on release.
Quarterly access reviews with owners.
Monitor activity logs for unusual access.

levels: People publish from Desktop to production.
Separate test workspace for some items.
Dev/Test/Prod with deployment pipelines for certified content; PBIP in Git.
Pull requests, automated checks (BPA, tests) and rollback for all production content.
Release metrics tracked; failure rate and lead time improve.
next: Create Dev/Test/Prod for the most-used models.
Put certified models in Git as PBIP with pipelines.
Add PR review and automated checks.
Track change failure rate and time to restore.
Keep improving the release process.

dims.q: How do you know something is wrong?
levels: Users tell us.
Refresh failure emails to individual owners.
Alerts to a team for certified models; capacity metrics checked.
SLOs for refresh and performance; usage reviewed monthly.
Proactive: trends predict problems before users see them.
next: Route failure notifications to a team mailbox.
Define severity levels and on-call for certified models.
Set refresh and performance SLOs; review monthly.
Trend capacity and refresh duration to plan ahead.
Keep it and share the learning.

levels: Not validated.
Spot checks before big meetings.
Reconciliations and data tests for certified models.
Automated tests in the pipeline; contracts with source teams.
Quality metrics published; issues fixed at the source.
next: Write a reconciliation for the top KPIs.
Automate data tests (row counts, uniqueness, totals).
Agree data contracts with source owners.
Publish quality metrics next to the KPIs.
Keep it.

tasks: Pick the two next steps with the best value for effort, and say who would own them.

deliverables.t: Top two next steps with owners and dates

hints: Score what's true for most of the estate, not for the BI team's showcase model.

rubric.good: Each score is backed by a fact from the inventory or experience, not by aspiration.
Next steps chosen for value and effort; owners named.
Can be presented in two minutes.
